hints.junior: A test that pads a real wait to "probably be enough" is still gambling on how busy the CI runner is that day.
hints.mid: If a test only fails on shared CI runners and never locally, a real-timer race is the first thing to suspect, not a product bug.
hints.staff: The fix isn't a longer padding value — it's removing the real wait from the test's critical path entirely.

hints.junior: Watch the fake-timer version assert zero calls before advancing the clock, then exactly one call right after — no waiting either time.
hints.mid: advanceTimersByTime(300) is exact; the real-timer version's 350ms is a guess at how much CI jitter to absorb.
hints.staff: Exact timer advancement caught a real off-by-one in the debounce comparison that the padded real-timer version had been silently absorbing.

hints.junior: Fake timers swap out setTimeout for a version the test itself controls — advancing it fires callbacks instantly, no real waiting.
hints.mid: vi.advanceTimersByTime / jest.advanceTimersByTime fires everything due in that window synchronously, including timers that schedule further timers.
hints.staff: This only removes timer-race flakiness — network calls, unflushed microtasks, and layout timing can still flake for unrelated reasons.

hints.junior: Always call useRealTimers() after a test that faked them, usually in afterEach, or the fake clock leaks into the next test file.
hints.mid: Fake timers don't automatically fake requestAnimationFrame — check your library's toFake option if a component also depends on rAF timing.
hints.staff: waitFor's own internal polling can stall against a fake clock; use your library's async-flush helper (e.g. advanceTimersByTimeAsync) when combining the two.

sections.junior: Hey! This one's about a test that passes on your laptop every time but flakes in CI once in a while. Turns out it's racing a real clock, not testing your code.
sections.mid: We're looking at why a real setTimeout wait inside a test becomes a coin flip under CI load, and how fake timers fix that.
sections.staff: This covers fake-timer libraries, exact clock advancement, and where fake timers stop helping.

sections.junior: A fake-timer library swaps out setTimeout with one the test controls. Advancing it fires callbacks right away, no real waiting.
sections.mid: vi.advanceTimersByTime fires everything due in that window synchronously, in order.
sections.staff: This fixes timer races specifically. It won't help with network calls or layout-timing flakiness.

sections.junior: Look at the two tests side by side. The flaky one pads its wait and hopes. The fake-timer one advances the clock to the exact millisecond.
sections.mid: Notice the fake-timer version can assert the zero-calls state before advancing — the real-timer version can't cheaply do that.
sections.staff: Exact advancement is what caught the off-by-one debounce comparison in the story above.

sections.junior: If a test only flakes in CI, suspect a real-timer race before anything else.
sections.mid: Fake timers make timer-dependent tests deterministic and fast — no real waiting, no CI-load guessing.
sections.staff: Clean up with useRealTimers() every time, and reach for your library's async-flush helper when mixing fake timers with waitFor.
